justification: The ledger polices a declared status in both directions -- fixed-but-failing and open-but-passing both go red -- for every row that HAS a check. A row declared open with `check: null` is the one state it cannot see: it can rot, be silently fixed, or be quietly wrong, and nothing says so. Five rows sat there. This closes that blind spot to zero and lowers the ratchet so it cannot reopen. Critical because a check written wrong is worse than none -- it sends someone to repair working code -- and three of the five detectors here were wrong on their first draft.

pre_impl.existing_data: Read-only throughout; no statement in this change writes. dcp_plan_as_at (23 columns, 28 rows, keyed by `lga` -- which is DQ-43's premise, confirmed not assumed), dcp_chapter_registry, regulatory_provisions, information_schema. `url_page_last_status` confirmed ABSENT, which is what DQ-58's own note prescribed building.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Five, and three changed the code. (1) DQ-31: I assumed both implementations spelled the gate `isLMRArea`; the Python service spells it `in_lmr_area`, so the one file that matters was missed while two irrelevant ones were reported. (2) DQ-31 again: `isLMRArea?: boolean` -- TypeScript's optional-property marker -- matched a pattern meant for ternaries, so a presentational component counted as an implementation of a regulated decision. (3) DQ-53: my first detector looked for a live call shaped like `.to_dict(` and accused three working tests, two of which call a plain function and a classmethod. (4) DQ-43: ku_ring_gai looked like a live instance of the defect -- two plan names, renders a date -- and is not; the names are one plan registered three ways, checked against the council's own document tree before reporting it. (5) The regex escapes were mangled through nested shell heredocs into literal \x08 backspace characters, which grep renders invisibly; the file was deleted and rewritten rather than patched.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new mechanism. The probe copies dq_probe_live.py's contract exactly (exit 0 only at zero, exit 2 when the source is unreachable, every number prints its own derivation) and is a sibling of dq_probe_applicability_config.py in shape. It is a separate file because dq_probe_live.py is SQL-only by construction -- its PROBES map holds a SQL string the runner executes -- and two of these five are static analyses of the repo.
pre_impl.external_source_error: None. DQ-58 deliberately does NOT fetch by default: nine council websites in CI's dependency graph, three behind Cloudflare which 403s automated clients, is a check that goes red for reasons unrelated to the defect and then gets deleted. The default asks whether the recording instrument exists; `--live` fetches on demand.
pre_impl.frontend_type: One route changed: app/api/dcp-review/route.ts. It gains the same denyIfUnauthenticated() its two sibling write routes already carry (no-op unless NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED is 'true', so it cannot lock anyone out of an environment that does not run auth), stops returning the driver's error text to the caller, and orders the queue by fidelity SEVERITY instead of testing one status value. No type changes: the row shape the UI consumes is unchanged, and the new ORDER BY is a CASE over an existing column.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A defect sits open for months while the ledger reports nothing, because the row tracking it has no check. Or -- worse, and the risk this change itself carried -- a check fires on correct code and someone repairs a working test.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: any unresolved ledger row has no check, or a declared status disagrees with what its check just returned. `_max_unverified_unresolved` is now 0, so adding a row without a check fails immediately rather than in six months.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before: 5 unresolved rows with `check: null` (DQ-31, DQ-42, DQ-43, DQ-53, DQ-58) and `_max_unverified_unresolved: 3`. After: 0, cap lowered to 0, `_max_no_check` 48 -> 43. The ratchet tests failed on the un-lowered caps and were the thing that demanded it.
falsifiable_check.manual_probe: python scripts/dq_probe_unchecked_rows.py --id DQ-31  (and 42, 43, 53, 58). Reads 1, 0, 2, 0, 25 respectively on 2026-09-23.

functions.name: probe_31
functions.input: Nothing; it walks frontend-nextjs and services under the module's ROOT.
functions.output: (copies beyond the first, {(path, ''): 1}) for files that APPLY the LMR gate to produce an eligibility verdict.
functions.if_none: A file that merely NAMES the gate is not an implementation -- a comment quoting old code, a prop declaration and an object-literal pass-through all exist in this repo and all three were wrongly counted by the first draft. Counting them would also make consolidation unreachable: the number could never fall to zero however much was merged, which is a ratchet that measures nothing.

functions.name: probe_53
functions.input: Nothing; it parses every tests/test_*.py under the module's ROOT with ast.
functions.output: (count, {(path, funcname): 1}) for contract tests that load a stored artefact and never call into the project.
functions.if_none: 'Calls into the project' is resolved from the module's own imports of services/ src/ enrichment/ scripts/, not from a list of call shapes. Enumerating shapes is a way of missing one, and the miss accuses a working test -- the harmful direction.

functions.name: probe_43
functions.input: An open read-only cursor against the production database; the query and its scope are written inside the function, not passed in.
functions.output: (count, {(council, detail): 1}) for served councils whose current rows span more than one plan NAME.
functions.if_none: It measures the precondition, not the harm, and says so: a council with several names for one plan is indistinguishable from a genuine two-plan council, which is exactly why the plan-identity model cannot be built yet. It also declares its own blind spot -- 7,254 of 20,261 served rows carry a NULL source_chapter_key and drop out of the registry join.

functions.name: reversed_text_tokens
functions.input: One provision's text, which may be None or empty for a removal row.
functions.output: The tokens the reader emitted backwards, evidenced by their own reversal being a word this domain uses.
functions.if_none: Empty input yields []. A token counts only when its reversal is in _PLANNING_WORDS AND the token itself is not, so a palindrome ('level', 'civic') can never fire and an ordinary reversible English pair ('drawer'/'reward') is not in the vocabulary at all. classify_row_fidelity then requires TWO DISTINCT such tokens: one can be a surname or an acronym, two is a reading direction.

functions.name: _urls_not_in_source
functions.input: The council's own text from one row, and the whole chapter's extracted text.
functions.output: Sorted distinct HOSTS the row cites that appear nowhere in the chapter.
functions.if_none: An empty chapter returns [] -- no source URLs means no basis for comparison, and accusing every URL because the source text failed to extract would fire hardest on the rows already in trouble. A host the source carries in truncated form is accepted by a prefix test in either direction: a line wrap that eats `au/...` is a broken link, not an invented source.

values.name: DQ-31 counts copies BEYOND the first
values.why: One implementation of a regulated decision is the target state, not a defect. Counting files instead would make the check unsatisfiable, and an unsatisfiable ratchet gets ignored.
values.source: services/housing_sepp_eligibility.py's own docstring: it PORTS the gate logic from the frontend route, 'the only prior implementation', and records that 'the LEP/SEPP tab migrates onto it (P3)' is outstanding.
values.if_missing: The count reads one higher than the truth forever and can never reach zero, so nobody acts on it.

values.name: The ternary alternative excludes `?:`
values.why: TypeScript's optional-property marker is `isLMRArea?: boolean`. A bare `\?` reads that as the start of a ternary, and that one character made HousingSEPPEligibilityCard.tsx -- which declares the flag as a prop and passes it through -- count as an implementation of the eligibility decision.
values.source: Measured 2026-09-23: the count read 2 with the bare `\?` and 1 without.
values.if_missing: Any component that accepts the flag as an optional prop is reported as a second copy of the decision, so the count can never fall to zero.

values.name: DQ-58's default asks for the instrument, not the answer
values.value: count of distinct active page URLs when url_page_last_status does not exist
values.why: The row prescribes a stored status written by the monitor, then a probe over the column. The column does not exist, so the honest measurement is how many URLs have no recorded status -- a number that can only fall by building the recording.
values.source: Measured 2026-09-23: information_schema has no url_page_last_status on dcp_chapter_registry; 25 distinct council_page_url values on active chapters.
values.if_missing: Defaulting to a live fetch puts nine council sites in CI, three behind Cloudflare. A check red for reasons unrelated to the defect gets deleted, which is how this row ended up with no check in the first place.

values.name: _max_unverified_unresolved lowered to 0
values.why: The cap exists so the blind spot can only shrink. At 0 it becomes a hard floor: a new unresolved row without a check fails the ratchet immediately.
values.source: Measured after wiring: 29 unresolved rows, 0 without a check. The ratchet tests failed on the old cap of 3 and are what demanded the change.
values.if_missing: The cap stays above reality and a row can be added with no check without anything noticing -- the exact state this change closed.

values.name: The reversed-text threshold is two DISTINCT tokens
values.why: One hit can be a genuine token that happens to mirror a planning word. Two independent ones in the same provision is a page read right-to-left. Counting OCCURRENCES rather than distinct words would let one repeated figure label trip the gate on its own.
values.source: All five instances found by the crude probe carry three or more; the full-corpus scan with the real detector found 27 served rows, every one with two or more.
values.if_missing: At a threshold of one, an ordinary provision containing a single mirrored-looking token is auto-REJECTED and a real control is thrown away.

values.name: The URL check matches HOST, not the whole URL
values.why: The path is where extraction damage is most common and least consequential -- a wrapped line loses a segment and the link breaks. A wrong DOMAIN is a citation to somebody else entirely, which is the thing worth failing on.
values.source: Measured 2026-09-23 against the real row: the council's PDF carries epa.nsw.gov.au and penrithcity.nsw.gov.au; the row carried epa.ny.gov.gov.uk and pernitchlq.nsw.gov.au.
values.if_missing: Whole-URL matching flags every line-wrapped citation in the corpus, and a check that cries wolf on ordinary extraction damage is switched off within a week.

queries.purpose: Confirm DQ-43's premise rather than assume it: is dcp_plan_as_at really keyed by LGA?
queries.where_clause: information_schema.columns for dcp_plan_as_at -- 23 columns, primary key `lga`, 28 rows.

queries.purpose: Size the join's blind spot before relying on it.
queries.where_clause: regulatory_provisions WHERE is_current AND v2_is_actionable -- 7,254 of 20,261 carry a NULL source_chapter_key and drop out of the registry join; 13,007 join. Stated in probe_43's docstring rather than hidden.

queries.purpose: Timeout risk on the heaviest query.
queries.where_clause: Execution Time 59.043 ms. No batching needed; well inside the 30s statement timeout.

break_it.scenario: A detector is written that cannot fire, and its 0 is read as clean.
break_it.what_happens: DQ-53 reads 0 on this repo. Without evidence that it CAN report something else, that is indistinguishable from a pattern that matches nothing -- which is the '0% drift' verification the ledger's own README names as worse than no check.
break_it.how: A synthetic fixture-only contract test is planted in a tmp tree and asserted to be CAUGHT, beside two confusable negatives that must not fire.

break_it.scenario: The DQ-53 detector enumerates live-call SHAPES instead of asking whether the project is called.
break_it.what_happens: It accuses working tests. Measured: three false positives on this suite, two of which call a plain function and a classmethod that the shape list did not name. Someone then 'repairs' a correct test.
break_it.how: Resolution is by import: any call whose root name was imported from services/ src/ enrichment/ scripts/ counts. The three real false positives are pinned by name against the real suite, not a fixture.

break_it.scenario: A prop declaration is counted as a decision.
break_it.what_happens: `isLMRArea?: boolean` matches a ternary pattern, so a presentational component is reported as a second implementation of a regulated eligibility decision and the count can never reach zero.
break_it.how: `\?(?!:)`, pinned by test_a_prop_declaration_is_not_an_implementation.

break_it.scenario: A caller that forwards to the service is counted as a copy.
break_it.what_happens: Consolidation becomes unreachable -- the thing the fix produces (a delegating frontend) would still read as a defect.
break_it.how: Delegation names the fields without applying the gate; pinned as a confusable negative.

break_it.scenario: DQ-43's count is read as 'these councils serve two plans'.
break_it.what_happens: ku_ring_gai gets reported as a live instance of a defect the row says is not live. It nearly was: two names, renders a date. Checked against the council's own document tree, they are Section A and Section B of ONE plan registered three ways.
break_it.how: The probe's docstring and the ledger note both say what the number is -- a precondition, an ambiguity -- and name ku_ring_gai as the case that is NOT the harm.

break_it.scenario: DQ-43's join silently ignores a third of the corpus.
break_it.what_happens: 7,254 of 20,261 served rows have a NULL source_chapter_key. A council serving a second plan entirely through key-less rows reads clean.
break_it.how: Not closed. Stated in the probe's docstring and the ledger note, with the fix named: give those rows a chapter key, do not loosen the join. Loosening it would trade a stated blind spot for an unstated wrong answer.

break_it.scenario: DQ-58 is 'fixed' by making the live fetch the default.
break_it.what_happens: CI depends on nine council websites, three behind Cloudflare. The check goes red for reasons unrelated to the defect and is deleted -- which is how this row came to have no check at all.
break_it.how: The default reads the column; --live is explicit and opt-in. The row's own note records the reasoning so the next person does not re-derive it.

break_it.scenario: DQ-58 is 'fixed' by deleting the page URLs.
break_it.what_happens: The count falls to zero and every citation link is gone.
break_it.how: passes_when says it outright: reachable only by the monitor writing the status, never by removing the URLs. Not guarded in code; guarded by the as-at coverage check, which needs those URLs to derive an 'observed current' basis.

break_it.scenario: DQ-31 is 'fixed' by deleting the Python service.
break_it.what_happens: The count falls to zero by removing the consolidation's single source of truth, leaving the frontend copy as the only implementation -- the state DQ-31 was opened against.
break_it.how: passes_when names the direction: reachable only by the route delegating to the service. Not enforced in code; the service's own tests would go with it and the capacity brief ceiling derives from it.

break_it.scenario: A row is added to the ledger later with no check.
break_it.what_happens: The blind spot reopens silently, exactly as it did for these five over several months.
break_it.how: _max_unverified_unresolved lowered 3 -> 0, so the ratchet fails on the first such row. _max_no_check lowered 48 -> 43 in the same move.

break_it.scenario: A regex is written through nested shell escaping.
break_it.what_happens: `\b` became a literal \x08 backspace in the source. grep renders it invisibly, so the file LOOKED correct while every word boundary was a control character and the pattern matched nothing. The probe read 0 and would have been committed as clean.
break_it.how: The file was deleted and rewritten through the editor rather than patched through a heredoc, and checked for control bytes afterwards. This repo already has tests/test_ledger_has_no_control_chars.py for the same class.
break_it.repro: python -c "import io;print([c for c in (8,11,12,27) if bytes([c]) in io.open('scripts/dq_probe_unchecked_rows.py','rb').read()])"

break_it.scenario: The registry join is slow enough to be killed by the statement timeout.
break_it.what_happens: The probe exits non-zero for an infrastructure reason, which the ledger reads as the defect being present -- a check red for the wrong reason, and the shape that got DQ-58 deleted before it was ever written.
break_it.how: Measured before shipping rather than assumed: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) over the three-table join returns Execution Time 59.043 ms against the full served set. Two orders of magnitude inside the 30s statement timeout, so no batching.

break_it.scenario: The DB-backed probes are run with psycopg2 stubbed by conftest_mocks.py.
break_it.what_happens: cur.fetchall() returns a MagicMock, so probe_42 and probe_43 iterate nothing and report 0, and probe_58 compares a mock to an int. A probe that never touched a row reports the same 'clean' as one that did.
break_it.how: A @pytest.mark.database file asserts each SQL parses against the live schema, that DQ-43's three-table join matches a non-empty slice, that DQ-58 takes the branch production dictates rather than a flag, and that each exit code matches its own printed count.

break_it.scenario: probe_43's stated blind spot is quietly fixed upstream and the caveat rots.
break_it.what_happens: The docstring keeps warning that 7,254 served rows have no chapter key long after they all do, so a future reader distrusts a number that is now complete -- a stale caveat is its own defect.
break_it.how: test_dq43_states_its_blind_spot_rather_than_hiding_it FAILS when no served row lacks a chapter key, and its message says to delete the paragraph rather than leave it.
break_it.repro: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 python -m pytest -m database tests/test_dq_probe_unchecked_rows_real_db.py -k blind_spot -o addopts=

break_it.scenario: Worst-first sorting tests one status value instead of ranking severity.
break_it.what_happens: `ORDER BY (fidelity_status = 'flagged') DESC` puts flagged rows on top and leaves 'failed' -- which is WORSE, the gate could not match the row to its source page at all -- sorted among the unchecked bulk. Measured 2026-09-23 while re-grading: 3 of the first 9 rows needing a person were 'failed' and sat below ~490 rows that needed nobody.
break_it.how: A CASE ranking failed < flagged < ungraded < grounded, so a new status added later falls into the middle (unknown) rather than silently to the bottom.
break_it.repro: GET /api/dcp-review and read the first rows' fidelity_status

break_it.scenario: An internal READ route ships with the auth check on its page only.
break_it.what_happens: The whole pending queue -- council chapter names, every provision's old and new text, the gate's verdicts -- is readable by anyone who knows the path. Same shape as app/api/internal/pipeline-status, found the same day.
break_it.how: The route now carries the same guard as its two sibling WRITE routes, and the catch logs the detail server-side while returning a fixed string.
break_it.repro: NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED=true, request /api/dcp-review with no session cookie -- expect 401.

break_it.scenario: The reversed-text detector is written as a substring probe.
break_it.what_happens: Looking for 'kcabtes'/'nimm'/'xamm' as substrings matched 40 served rows on 2026-09-23 of which 35 were FALSE POSITIVES -- those letter runs occur inside ordinary words. As an auto-REJECT that discards real controls.
break_it.how: Token-level and evidence-based: the reversal must be a word this domain uses and the token itself must not be. Verified against the full served corpus, not a sample: 20,261 rows scanned, 27 hits.

break_it.scenario: The vocabulary is swapped for a general English dictionary.
break_it.what_happens: English is full of words that reverse into other words -- drawer/reward, straw/warts, desserts/stressed -- and palindromes reverse into themselves. Ordinary prose starts auto-rejecting.
break_it.how: A small domain vocabulary, with eleven ordinary reversible/palindromic words pinned as tests that must NOT fire.

break_it.scenario: The probe and the enqueue gate drift apart.
break_it.what_happens: The number the ledger reports stops describing the rule the pipeline enforces, so a row can read clean in one and dirty in the other.
break_it.how: The probe IMPORTS reversed_text_tokens from dcp_extract_changed; there is one vocabulary.

break_it.scenario: A row that DELETES a mirrored provision is auto-rejected.
break_it.what_happens: The removal row carries the mirrored text it exists to remove, so the clean-up is rejected and the chapter freezes -- measured 2026-09-18 on junk_ref, where two such rows held a 105-row chapter.
break_it.how: change_type != 'removed', the same exemption junk_ref and emptied_by_strip carry, pinned as a test.

break_it.scenario: A newly onboarded council ships with no applicability config.
break_it.what_happens: Its rules apply to every development type by fallthrough. DQ-33 counts the same defect globally against a floor of 1,158 and read 924 on 2026-09-23 -- 234 rows of headroom -- so the new council hides inside it and nothing goes red. Everything else a new council meets is universal; this is the one onboarding step nothing can derive.
break_it.how: DQ-105 is per-council and has no floor. It counts COUNCILS rather than rows, because how many of a council's rows fall through depends on whether the text regex happened to match and moves on every re-extraction.

break_it.scenario: A check about the tagger asks a question ADJACENT to the tagger's own.
break_it.what_happens: DQ-105 got this wrong twice in one afternoon. It compared `source_council` to the config registry while the tagger keys on `document_id`, so Inner West -- the most deeply configured council in the product -- was reported as having no config, on 11 rows that are Marrickville and Ashfield plans carrying the parent slug. Corrected to call the tagger, it then passed an EMPTY provision text, and Waverley and Woollahra key on a section code read out of that text, so Waverley was reported as unconfigured while serving 392 rows with zero fallthrough.
break_it.how: Resolved per ROW, calling the tagger's own entry points with that row's own text. Six configured councils are pinned as must-never-appear against the live corpus, beside a confusable negative asserting the probe still names parramatta -- a resolver that matched everything would silence it entirely and read the same as 'all configured'.
break_it.repro: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 python -m pytest -m database tests/test_dq_probe_unchecked_rows_real_db.py -k DQ105 -o addopts=

break_it.scenario: The reader invents a citation by completing a damaged URL into a plausible one.
break_it.what_happens: It takes a real URL from a damaged scan and completes it into something plausible -- epa.nsw.gov.au became epa.ny.gov.gov.uk, penrithcity.nsw.gov.au became pernitchlq.nsw.gov.au -- and the fidelity gate could not see it, because it checks numbers and words and a URL is neither. A fabricated citation passed a gate built to catch fabrication.
break_it.how: _urls_not_in_source compares the row's hosts against the whole chapter's and takes the row to flagged. Both real inventions are pinned as tests, beside five kinds of ordinary extraction damage that must NOT fire.

break_it.scenario: A council's config is written from its Part TITLES.
break_it.what_happens: Penrith 'D2 Residential Development' reads residential-only and is not: its own contents include 2.6 NON RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENTS. Declaring the residential types deletes that section from every non-residential application it governs -- the same defect as canterbury_bankstown 9.1, which was configured industrial by its position in the numbering.
break_it.how: All eight scopes are quoted from the Part's own scope section in its PDF, and each test carries the quotation. penrith_d2 decides NEITHER key as a result.

break_it.scenario: A whole-DCP council is 'fixed' by splitting its PDF and re-extracting.
break_it.what_happens: Re-extraction risks what dcp_commit_approved's section-loss guard exists to catch -- a re-read has gutted a chapter before -- and changes every affected provision's provenance, to recover structure the data already holds.
break_it.how: The Part is already in each rule's own section reference; the EXISTING `parts` path reads it and strips progressively (G9.1 -> G9 -> G). Measured: a code is readable on 1,560 of 1,602 Warringah rows, and the config took rows applying to every development type from 1,535 to 237 with no new code.

break_it.scenario: The retag runs without the LGA's zone list, so the DQ-30 filter is bypassed.
break_it.what_happens: Warringah DCP 2011 predates the 2022 employment-zone reform and names B1, B2, B5, B6 and B7 throughout. The text regex picked them up and the retag NARROWED 34 served rows onto zone codes that no longer exist -- wrong, and an immediate OC-17 failure on its retired-zone sub-check.
break_it.how: build_plan now loads lep_zone_coverage per LGA and passes valid_zones, so an absent code is filtered to ALL rather than narrowed onto. Narrowings fell 135 -> 92 and every remaining shape is in a chapter whose scope statement was read. Returns None (do not filter) for a council with no coverage, because silently dropping every zone would look like a successful narrowing.
break_it.repro: python scripts/retag_applicability_slug_docids.py --councils northern_beaches blacktown penrith hornsby georges_river

break_it.scenario: A config declares a Part precinct-scoped and the `parts` path discards it.
break_it.what_happens: `_get_config_driven`'s parts branch called `_from_entry(entry)` without is_precinct_specific, so the declaration never arrived. The config file looks correct and the flag is gone -- the same defect already fixed in the chapter_topics branch, left live in this one. waverley_config.py declares it on Part E 'Site-Specific Provisions' today.
break_it.how: The parts branch now carries it through, matching chapter_topics and the ashfield/leichhardt paths. Found by a test written for the new config failing against the OLD code path. ⚠ Inert today: nothing downstream consumes the flag from the tagger's output, and DQ-99's guard reads a different column.

break_it.scenario: The approve script writes during what the operator asked to be a dry run.
break_it.what_happens: It is pointed at the table that decides what reaches a planner, and the last bulk approval on this queue put 578 bad rows live. A tool that writes when told not to is worse than one that refuses to write at all.
break_it.how: A @pytest.mark.database test runs the real script against the real queue and asserts the FULL status census is unchanged -- a census rather than a pending count, so a row moved between two other statuses would still show. Under the stubbed driver the plan is empty and prints 'to approve: 0', which reads exactly like an already-clear queue, so this cannot be tested offline.
break_it.repro: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 python -m pytest -m database tests/test_dcp_approve_graded_real_db.py -k dry -o addopts=

post_merge.db_reset: None. Every query in this change is read-only.
post_merge.secrets: None added. DQ-42, DQ-43 and DQ-58 use the DATABASE_URL the ledger already needs.
post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/dq_check.py --coverage (expect OK across all 106 rows), then python -c on dq_checks.json to confirm 0 unresolved rows without a check.
